Bug_Details:
In Java, the Object.equals() method is used for object comparison, and it is typically overridden in classes to provide a custom
equality check based on your criteria for equality.
The default implementation of equals() provided by the Object class compares the memory references of the two objects,
that means it checks if the objects are actually the same instance in memory.
The "equals" as a method name should be used exclusively to override Object.equals(Object) to prevent confusion.
It is important to note that when you override equals() , you should also override the hashCode() method to maintain the
contract between equals() and hashCode() .
Bug_Explanation: The equals method is overridden to accept a parameter of type CustomEquality instead of Object. This breaks the contract specified by Object.equals(Object), leading to potential issues when using instances of CustomEquality with collections or APIs that rely on Object's equals method.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered because the CustomEquality class incorrectly overrides the equals method to accept a parameter of type CustomEquality instead of Object. This breaks the contract of Object.equals(Object). The tests fail when attempting to compare CustomEquality objects with other types or null, which should be handled gracefully by a correctly overridden equals method.
